newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Foreningsbanken lower loan losses boost Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: Foreningsbanken lower loan losses boost Q1 profit.

text.p: Swedish bank Foreningsbanken on Tuesday posted a 24 percent rise in first quarter operating profit after loan losses to 278 million crowns ($35.6 million), thanks to increased income and lower loan losses.
"Increased volumes for both deposits and lending as well as falling volumes for problem loans helped strengthen net interest income," the bank said.

Foreningsbanken, which is merging with Swedbank to form one of Sweden's largest banking groups, said loan losses fell 30 percent to 190 million crowns while problem loans dropped 36 percent to 1.9 billion crowns.
Deposits rose two percent to 63.4 billion crowns and lending increased 15 percent to 90.9 billion. Assets under management surged 70 percent to 15.9 billion crowns.
Net commission increased 28 percent to 226 million crowns, mainly boosted by fund operations but also by payment services and lending.
On the negative side, the bank noted net financial transactions swinging to a charge of 44 million crowns from a credit of 31 million.
In addition, costs rose seven percent to 746 million crowns, partly because of one-off items.
Net interest income amounted to 912 million crowns, up eight percent including the higher government charge for deposit guarantee and up 12 percent excluding it, the bank said in a statement.
